title: Healing After Birth Takes Weeks, Not Days
hook: Your body just did something huge, and recovery is a season, not a single appointment. Bleeding, cramps, healing, and mood shifts are all part of the fourth trimester.
key_points: Vaginal bleeding (lochia) is heavy at first, then fades over several weeks — but tell your midwife about large clots.
Afterpains, a sore perineum or stitches, and a healing c-section wound are normal and ease day by day.
Rest when you can and lean on support; recovery is physical and emotional, and it takes time.
Postpartum care is an ongoing process, not just the 6-week check — reach out between visits if something feels off.
content_html: Birth is a major physical event, and recovering from it is a season — often called the fourth trimester — not something that wraps up at one appointment. In the first weeks you can expect vaginal bleeding (lochia) that's heavy at first and fades over several weeks, cramping afterpains as your womb shrinks back down, and a tender perineum, stitches, or a healing c-section wound.
extra_html: The NHS describes this gradual healing as normal: bleeding turns brownish and tapers off, afterpains ease day by day, and a sore perineum or stitches improve with gentle care like bathing in plain warm water. Rest when you can, accept help with the basics, and remember that recovery is emotional as well as physical. Postpartum care is meant to be ongoing — not just a single six-week check — so reach out to your midwife or doctor between visits if anything feels off, and especially for large blood clots. This is general guidance — reach out to your doctor or midwife with any concerns; if you have thoughts of harming yourself or the baby, seek help immediately.

related.title: Warning Signs That Can't Wait
related.hook: Serious complications can happen during pregnancy and for up to a year after birth. Knowing the urgent warning signs — and insisting on being heard — can save a life.

related.title: Baby Blues or Something More?
related.hook: Weepy and overwhelmed in the first days is common and usually passes within two weeks. When low mood lingers and disrupts daily life, it may be postpartum depression — common and treatable.

flashcards.prompt: What's normal for vaginal bleeding (lochia) after birth?

choices.text: Heavy at first, gradually fading over several weeks
It stops completely within a day or two
Large clots are expected and nothing to mention

flashcards.explanation_html: Lochia is heavy early on and slowly turns brownish and lighter over weeks. Large clots, though, are worth telling your midwife about.

flashcards.prompt: Is the 6-week checkup the whole of postpartum care?
flashcards.back_html: No. Recovery is an ongoing process over roughly the first 12 weeks. You can and should reach out to your provider between visits if something feels wrong.

flashcards.prompt: Which of these are normal parts of early postpartum recovery?

choices.text: Afterpains, a sore perineum/stitches, and a healing c-section wound
No bleeding at all after a vaginal birth

flashcards.explanation_html: Cramping afterpains, perineal soreness or stitches, and a healing surgical wound are all expected and tend to improve day by day.
